reasons: Both answers correct the two false premises in their opening lines. Both say a replacement can be done in Guangzhou, and that 12306's e-certificate (24 hours, 6 per month) or a station paper proof gets the user on the train on 10/31 without going home. Both give 40 yuan for the replacement, 10 yuan and 3 months for the temporary ID, and the 5-working-day wait for the household-registration office, so the temporary ID is unlikely to arrive before 10/31. Both also say the paper proof is free, which the key flags as unsupported, and neither gives the 60-day legal limit; both give Guangzhou's 40 days instead. I confirmed on the Liwan page that 40 days and the 40 yuan fee are real. I confirmed on the Zhengzhou page that the in-province limit is 15 working days, so B's quoted figure holds, and the date arithmetic in both answers checks out. B edges ahead because it names the July 2017 nationwide rollout, states the 20 yuan renewal fee, says to apply for the e-certificate within 24 hours of travel, and tells the user to ask at the counter whether the temporary ID can be ready by 10/31. It is also a little tighter. A has more unverifiable 12306 and self-service details and repeats itself with a table and extra sections, though it is very actionable.
